title: Maximum Sum of Alternating Subsequence With Distance at Least K
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the maximum sum of a strictly alternating subsequence where the difference between consecutive indices is at least k.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, find the maximum sum of a strictly alternating subsequence where the difference between consecutive indices is at least k. A subsequence of length 1 is also valid. The score is the sum of the selected values.
constraints: nums contains positive integers and k is positive.
Choose indices at least k apart whose adjacent selected values strictly alternate up and down.
A singleton is valid; maximize the sum.
hints: Track best sums ending after an upward or downward comparison.
Fenwick prefix maxima over value ranks find the best smaller predecessor; a reversed-rank tree finds larger predecessors.
Delay insertion until an index is at least k behind the current position.
Strict rank ranges enforce alternating inequalities, and delayed updates enforce distance while every valid predecessor remains queryable.
editorial: Strict rank ranges enforce alternating inequalities, and delayed updates enforce distance while every valid predecessor remains queryable.

tests.explanation: Indices zero and two are two apart and decrease strictly, giving sum seven.
The whole sequence alternates up then down and sums six.
